data.title: Energy transport firm Vivakor's Q2 revenue rises, net loss narrows
data.description:
Overview

  • US energy transport and remediation firm's Q2 revenue rose 10% yr/yr on supply & trading growth

  • Gross profit for Q2 rose 45% and gross margin improved to 20.7%

  • Company returned to positive operating income, net loss narrowed 78% yr/yr

Outlook

  • Vivakor did not provide specific financial guidance for the current or future periods

Result Drivers

  • SUPPLY & TRADING EXPANSION - Co said Q2 revenue growth was mainly due to expansion of crude oil supply and trading activities

  • MIDSTREAM PROFITABILITY - Improved profitability across midstream operations contributed to higher gross margin

  • LOWER OPERATING EXPENSES - Operating expenses fell mainly due to reduced depreciation and amortization

data.title: REG - R8 Capital Inv. PLC - Result of AGM, Board, Fundraising and Sub-division
data.description:
RNS Number : 7352R R8 Capital Investments PLC 21 August 2026  

21 August 2026

R8 CAPITAL INVESTMENTS PLC

("R8", or the "Company")

RESULT OF ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING

BOARD CHANGES

£500,000 FUNDRAISING UPDATE

COMPLETION OF SUB-DIVISION

Annual General Meeting Result

R8 Capital Investments PLC, is pleased to announce that all of the Resolutions put before the Company's Annual General Meeting ("AGM") held today, 21 August 2026, at 10:00am were duly passed.

Fundraising Update

The Company is also pleased to confirm that, subject to receipt of funds, all other conditions to the £500,000 Fundraising via AlbR Capital, combining a Placing and a Subscription for a mixture of New Ordinary Shares and CLNs, have now been satisfied. Admission to trading of the Fundraising Shares is expected to occur as stipulated in the timetable set out in the Company's announcement of 20 August 2026.

The Company will provide a further update once the Fundraise has completed.

Board Changes

Following the passing of all the Resolutions at the AGM and subject to completion of the Fundraising, David Mason and Neil Jeffrey will be joining the Board as Non-Executive Directors and Jonathan Rowland and Richard Morecroft will resign from the Board.

Further information on David Mason

Directorships and further disclosures in relation to David Mason are as follows:

Current directorships / partnerships:

-     Sovereign International Limited

-     Lamera Capital Limited

Previous directorships / partnerships held within the last five years:

-     Aspire Payments Limited

-     Finseta Payment Solutions Limited

Save as set out above, there is no further information to be disclosed in respect of David Mason pursuant to UKLR 6.4.8R.

Further information on Neil Jeffrey

Current directorships / partnerships:

-     GCN Finance Limited

Previous directorships / partnerships held within the last five years:

-     Payment Assist (UK) Ltd

Save as set out above, there is no further information to be disclosed in respect of Neil Jeffrey pursuant to UKLR 6.4.8R.

Sub-division and Total Voting Rights

Following the passing of the Resolutions, and as a result of the Sub-division, there will be 107,411,062 Ordinary Shares of £0.0001 in issue and it is expected that admission to trading of the sub-divided Ordinary Shares will take place on 26 August 2026.

In accordance with DTR 5.6.1R of the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules, R8 announces that, the Company's issued share capital will consist of:

107,411,062 ordinary shares of £0.0001 each, each carrying one voting right.

The Company does not hold any ordinary shares in treasury.

Accordingly, the total number of voting rights in the Company as at the date of this announcement is 107,411,062.

The above figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine whether they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

Capitalised terms in this announcement shall have the same meaning as given in the Company's shareholder circular and notice of AGM dated 15 July 2026 and the Company's announcement of 20 August 2026.

The Directors of the Company accept responsibility for the contents of this announcement.

data.title: Wall St set for higher open but weekly losses loom
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 0.59%, S&P 0.46%, Nasdaq 0.69%
  • Crypto stocks surge as bitcoin hits over two-month high
  • Ross Stores gains after annual forecast raise

By Avinash P and Purvi Agarwal

The main U.S. indexes were set for a recovery on Friday after a pummeling in the previous session, though markets remained on track to end the week in the red as surging government bond yields and geopolitical tensions dampened risk appetite.

The S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq were set to snap a three-week winning streak, while the Dow was headed for a second consecutive weekly loss and its steepest weekly decline since mid-March.

A jump in long-dated U.S. Treasury yields spooked markets this week as concerns over ballooning government debt, higher financing costs and persistent inflation fears dented sentiment. The yield on the 30-year Treasury bond (US30YT=RR) hit its highest level since 2007 earlier this week.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday that the government could further increase its Treasury repurchases after Wednesday's surprise intervention.

Yields, however, remained near recent highs.

"Bond yields don't seem to be responding to the Treasury's purchases, largely because the bond market is massive and is pricing in a stronger economy and higher inflation," said Paul Stanley, managing director and founding advisor, Arca.

"It is another brick in the market's wall of worry and ultimately, the market will likely resume its focus on the promise of artificial intelligence and how companies are using this productivity to drive earnings."

Early on Friday, most megacaps were treading higher in premarket trading. Alphabet and Tesla led gains with a 0.6% and 1.2% rise, respectively, after Thursday's rout.

At 08:24 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) rose 312 points, or 0.59%, S&P 500 E-minis (EScv1) gained 35.5 points, or 0.46%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 202.75 points, or 0.69%.

In other movers, Ross Stores added 8% after the value retailer raised its annual profit forecasts and reported better-than-expected second-quarter results.

Crypto-linked companies continued to rise, with bitcoin touching its highest mark since late May after U.S. President Donald Trump called on Congress to pass a crucial crypto bill.

Exchange operator Coinbase Global gained 4.5%, bitcoin-hoarder Strategy rose 6.8% and retail-investor platform Robinhood advanced 4.8%.

Broader risk sentiment, however, remained in check as Bessent said the United States will impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran, a move he suggested would lessen the need for new major military operations.

The impasse between Washington and Tehran has kept oil prices elevated, though they dipped slightly on Friday.

UBS Global Wealth Management raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 to 8,100, pointing to a stronger earnings outlook and confidence that corporate profit growth will remain robust into next year.

A flash estimate of the S&P Global purchasing managers' index survey for August is scheduled for release after markets open.

EYES ON WARSH, AI BELLWETHER NVIDIA

Attention will now turn to next week's Personal Consumption Expenditures, the U.S. Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, following tame inflation readings last week that knocked down bets of an imminent central bank rate hike.

Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole symposium will also be watched for clues on the Fed's rate-cut trajectory.

Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings next week, in the next test of the AI trade following strong earnings from some AI infrastructure companies, along with major hyperscalers.

data.title: Crypto Stocks Keep Climbing in Tandem with Bitcoin
data.description:
By Dean Seal

U.S. stocks linked to cryptocurrencies look poised to extend this week's rally to Friday, climbing alongside Bitcoin following President Trump's recent show of support for crypto-friendly legislation.

Trump met with crypto industry executives this week to publicly urge Congress to pass the Clarity Act, which would establish a favorable regulatory framework for digital currencies. The bill has stalled in Congress, but is expected to go to the Senate floor for a vote next month.

Bitcoin rallied after Trump's comments, rising 21% over the past week to $76,774.30. It has gained 7% between Thursday and Friday mornings.

The president on Wednesday namechecked crypto exchange Hyperliquid Strategies, which has seen its stock surge more than 50% in the past week through Thursday's close. Shares were up another 1% at $10.18 in premarket trading.

Shares of the prominent exchange Coinbase were up 4.6% at $180.28 ahead of the opening bell. Crypto holding group Strategy's stock rose 6.8% to $120 and Mara Holdings was up 4.9% at $11.70.

Coinbase's chief executive, Brian Armstrong, was among the executives at Wednesday's meeting with Trump. He said in an interview on CNBC afterward that he was optimistic that the Clarity Act would be passed given Senate majority leader John Thune decision to put it to a floor vote in mid-September.

"[Thune] would not have scheduled this on Sept. 15 if he didn't think it would pass," Armstrong said.

Write to Dean Seal at dean.seal@wsj.com

data.title: Trump Signs Memo To Boost Space Transportation With Private Sector Partnership
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - President Donald Trump has signed a Presidential Memorandum to help drastically boost U.S. commercial space launches.

The Memorandum, which repeals an outdated National Space Transportation Policy, aims more than 1,000 rocket launches and reentries on American soil annually by 2030.

It directs agencies to incentivize co-development of space transportation infrastructure with private sector partners, expedite permitting and environmental reviews, develop fair and transparent cost recovery policies for common space services and infrastructure, and develop range scheduling criteria and publish range schedules to maximize allocation of launch resources.

The Memorandum directs the Secretary of Transportation and the Secretary of the Interior, in coordination with the Secretary of War and the Administrator of NASA, to identify future additional space transportation infrastructure locations, including additional launch and reentry sites. It also designates priority airspace for critical space launch corridors and integration of space transportation activities into air traffic control modernization efforts.

Under the Memo, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology has been directed to coordinate interagency efforts to develop and implement a space transportation industrial base strategy that promotes and maintains America's space transportation industry, streamlines procurement, and implements relevant space security strategies.

The Memorandum directs the NASA Administrator to facilitate commercial transportation to and from the moon, to facilitate commercial robotic access to Mars, and to explore commercial avenues to send humans to and from Mars.

The new policy will open new economic opportunities, such as high-paying aerospace manufacturing jobs and decrease the price for developing and deploying new space systems, according to the White House.

Enabling next-generation space capabilities will give Americans better positioning, navigation, and timing services for precision agriculture, more accurate weather forecasts for safe and predictable airline travel, and ubiquitous satellite-enabled communications for global broadband internet access, it added.

data.title: Gold's Rise Comes Amid New Phase in Capital Cycle — Market Talk
data.description: The recovery in gold prices reflects a shift away from U.S. Treasurys toward alternative assets amid uncertainty clouding the fixed income market and growing concerns about the sustainability of U.S. public debt, XS.com senior market analyst Samer Hasn says in a note. "I believe it is futile to discuss the potential paths for the yellow metal as a safe haven," he says. The Treasury Department's decision helped weaken the impact of high bond yields on gold and other non-yielding assets, "which might explain capital rotating back toward those assets." Flows into physical gold exchange-traded funds also helped fuel the upward trend, Hasn adds. Gold is up 1.5% at $4,639.80 an ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

data.title: Cryptocurrencies Haven't Turned a Corner Just yet — Market Talk
data.description: Cryptocurrencies are rallying on a flurry of positive catalysts, but it remains premature to call the start of a new bull run for the asset class, Jefferies's Andrew Moss writes. The rally in crypto tokens is driven by positive signals from U.S. regulators, and the Treasury's surprise move to increase its buybacks of longer-dated U.S. government bonds. However, the sharp increase in currencies is partly driven by short covering, with investors yet to show significant enthusiasm by buying into crypto. Bitcoin jumps 5.16% to $76,774.10, pairing some of the session's earlier gains. Ethereum gains 2.3% to $2,378.54. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Slip After Rising a Sixth Straight Month in June — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadians look to have reined in their retail spending last month following six straight months of rising purchases through June.

The value of retail trade in the country rose 0.6% in June from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 74.28 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$53.87 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday.

Yet an early tally of receipts indicates sales in July declined 0.8%, the first drop since the end of 2025. Sales growth in May was revised slightly higher to 1.1% from a prior 1% estimate.

The data agency's survey for June showed sales were up broadly, rising in seven of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by general merchandise stores. Compared with a year earlier, sales were up 5.2%.

The monthly advance, which was a touch stronger than the 0.4% growth economists had expected, meant sales over the second quarter increased 2.2%, or a more modest 0.4% in volume terms. It came as the wider economy has rebounded after a weak start to the year.

Statistics Canada offered no details with its forecast for July, which was based on the responses of more than half of retailers surveyed and will be revised.

Analysis of cardholder activity by Royal Bank of Canada, the country's largest lender, showed that consumers continued to spend through what was a challenging quarter, likely drawing on savings or taking on debt amid higher energy costs and weak wage gains. It found purchases of essentials excluding fuel grew for the period, while cardholder spending on discretionary goods recovered after a weak year and a half.

The rise in June sales came despite a drag from gasoline stations and fuel vendors, where receipts fell for the first time in four months as prices retreated. Stripping out fuel, retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% between June and July, Statistics Canada said.

Core sales, which exclude fuel as well as motor vehicles and parts, were up a third month running. For a second month that was led by sales at general merchandise retailers, which include super centers, warehouse clubs and the country's few remaining department stores.

Consumers also bought more at clothing, accessories, shoe, luggage and leather goods stores in June. The sole decrease in core sales was at food and drink retailers, a segment led by supermarkets and other grocery stores.

Canada's economy was growing in recent months and industry-level data points to annualized expansion of 3.4% in the second quarter, which would be the strongest in roughly three years and follows back-to-back quarterly contractions. The housing market and resale activity have picked up after faltering earlier in the year, jobs data shows a recovery in hiring, and surveys indicate businesses are adapting to a trade environment of uncertainty and U.S. tariffs.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: Iberdrola Inks Deal With RES To Boost Functioning Of 15 Onshore Wind Farms In UK
data.description:
BILBAO (dpa-AFX) - Iberdrola SA (IBDSF.PK, IBE1.DE, IBE.MC, 1IBE.MI), a Spanish electric utility company, said on Friday that its subsidiary, ScottishPower Renewables, has signed a five-year deal in July with RES, a renewable energy company, to boost the operation and maintenance of 15 onshore wind farms in the UK.

The contract will support a combined renewable capacity of nearly 600 MW. Together, the wind farms covered by the agreement have a capacity of 588 MW, enough to supply the equivalent of the annual electricity consumption of around 412,000 homes, according to Renewable Energy Systems, or RES.

data.title: Canadian Retail Sales Look to Fall for First Time This Year — Market Talk
data.description: A run of rising sales at Canadian retailers looks to have come to an end last month. Statistics Canada data showed retail sales increased 0.6% on-month in June, a touch stronger than the 0.4% advance economists expected. It comes after growth was revised up a tick for each of the prior three months. Still, an advance tally of receipts indicates sales declined 0.8% in July, which wold be the first decline in 2026. June's growth was driven by trade at general merchandise retailers, which more than made up for weaker sales at gas stations as fuel prices retreated during the month. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
